_why: A fixture that is not going to be played, named so the build can take it out. The `fixtures` table cannot be written from a developer machine - an anonymous write is refused with 42501, which is the posture working as designed - so a match called off on the Saturday would otherwise sit on the front page, in the countdown and on the programme until somebody is at a laptop with an admin session. Same device as match-corrections.json and fixtures-2627.json.
_retires: IT IS SAFE BECAUSE IT CANNOT DRIFT. A cancellation is matched on the fixture's own identity - the day and the two clubs, the same test dataset.mjs already uses to tell a fixture from its result - so it removes exactly that fixture and nothing else. The moment the club deletes the fixture in Control panel -> Fixtures it matches nothing and does nothing, so forgetting to delete it costs nothing. It can never cancel a match that has been played either: a result wins over a fixture before this is reached.
_retired: IT RETIRED ITSELF, AND THAT WAS CHECKED RATHER THAN ASSUMED. The one entry this file has ever held cancelled 18 Oct 2026, Sue's Angels FC v Mousa Mountain FC, after the club folded. While the stored fixture row existed, emptying this file changed 19 shipped pages. The club deleted that row in Control panel -> Fixtures on 19 October 2026, and emptying the file then changed NOTHING - index, fixtures, programme, league and news all byte for byte identical - which is the proof that the entry had stopped doing anything and was safe to take out. The mechanism stays for the next one; an empty list is it at rest. The club is still named under the League Eight table, which is `removed` in league-eight-2627.json and a different thing: that is a fact about the division, not about one match.
